images.title: Two thirds on the line
images.purpose: Show that a line from 0 to the second mark, when each unit is cut into 3 equal gaps, covers 2 gaps of 1/3 and is 2/3 unit long.
images.composition: One long number line low in the frame, a thick line on it from 0, and two small counting arcs above that line, all with wide white space.
images.exact_structure: A grey #6B7280 number line from 0 to 2 with exactly 7 evenly spaced ticks: each unit cut into 3 equal gaps. A thick teal #0072B2 line runs from 0 to the second tick after 0. Above it, exactly 2 equal amber #E69F00 arcs, one over each gap the teal line covers. The second tick after 0 is marked with a small reddish purple #CC79A7 dot. Exactly 1 number line, 1 teal line, 2 arcs.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
ticks that are not evenly spaced, or more than 2 counting arcs
images.takeaway: The line covers 2 gaps of 1/3, so it is 2/3 unit long.
images.description: A number line from 0 to 2 in thirds; a teal line from 0 to the second mark with 2 amber arcs counting the gaps; the first mark reads 1/3 and the second reads 2/3, with 2 × 1/3 = 2/3 above.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count the arcs, not the ticks, and say why the line is two thirds and not three thirds.

image_decisions.why: Counting gaps rather than marks is seen at a glance on one number line with counting arcs.
